newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy industry group Confapi to resume metal talks.
newsitem.headline: Italy industry group Confapi to resume metal talks.

text.p: The Italian employers group Confapi said on Friday that it would resume talks next week with engineering and metalworkers' unions to try to reach an accord in the industry's protracted pay dispute.
The organisation represents 12,000 companies accounting for more than 400,000 of the sector's 1.7 million employees.

Confapi president Luigi Garavaglia said in a statement that the organisation had accepted a request from the three trades unions, FIOM, FIM and UILM to resume negotiations. A precise time would be set by the parties.
"We hope negotiations will go rapidly and positively to restore calm to companies. Unions must make every effort," Garavaglia said.

Confapi represents small and medium-sized businesses and is one of three employers' groups in the sector, where the bitter pay dispute has been going on since last June. The largest organisation, Federmeccanica, has given no indication that it is ready to restart talks.
The dispute centres on the interpretation of a landmark 1993 wage deal, which scrapped automatic index linked wage rises.
Talks stalled last year. Federmeccanica has since rejected government proposals that workers should be given a 200,000 lire ($130) a month pay rise, to cover the 1996-98 contract period.
Unions, which originally asked for 230,000 lire a month, have accepted the proposal, but management has stuck to its 139,000 lire offer, saying any more would hit competitiveness.
"The trades unions must take account of the changed economic situation and of the relationship between the costs of renewing the contract and company balance sheets," Garavaglia said.
